reason: The text concludes with God's explicit blessing and covenant promises to Abraham. God swears (נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי) that He will bless Abraham abundantly, multiply his descendants as the stars in heaven, and ensure that 'all nations of the earth will be blessed through your seed' (וְהִתְבָּרֲכוּ בְזַרְעֲךָ כֹּל גּוֹיֵי הָאָרֶץ). These promises demonstrate commitment to the welfare of Abraham's descendants—the Hebrew people. Additionally, God provides a substitutionary ram, sparing Isaac's life. While the passage's primary narrative focuses on testing Abraham's faith and obedience, the divine blessing at its conclusion reveals that nurturing and protecting Abraham's lineage is indeed one of Yahweh's stated objectives.
